```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "../03.outputs/PNG/", dpi = 300, dev = "png")
fetch <- function(url, file) if (!file.exists(file)) {
  dir.create(dirname(file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  download.file(url, file, mode = "wb")
}
fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL) {
  df <- dplyr::mutate(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of("Year"), as.integer))
  right <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  flextable::flextable(df) |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(align = "center", part = "header") |>
    flextable::align(j = setdiff(names(df), right), align = "left", part = "body") |>
    flextable::align(j = right, align = "right", part = "body") |>
    flextable::colformat_int(big.mark = "") |>
    flextable::padding(padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1, part = "all") |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}
th <- ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 8) + ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
num <- \(x, d = 1) gsub("-(?=[0-9])", "−", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), round(x, d) + 0), perl = TRUE)
pm <- function(x, s, digits) dplyr::case_when(is.na(x) ~ "", is.na(s) ~ formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits),
  .default = paste0(formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits), " ± ", formatC(s, format = "f", digits = digits)))
msd <- \(x) sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f Mt CO~2~e a year (95 per cent confidence interval %.1f to %.1f)",
  mean(x), stats::sd(x), stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[1], stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[2])
u_term <- function(sd, mean) 1.96 * sd / mean
ci95 <- function(x) if (stats::sd(x) > 0) stats::t.test(x)$conf.int else c(mean(x), mean(x))
fmt_p <- \(p) if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste("=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
fmt_t <- function(fit, term) {
  s <- summary(fit)$coefficients[term, ]
  paste0("[t(", stats::df.residual(fit), ") = ", formatC(s[[3]], format = "f", digits = 3), ", p ", fmt_p(s[[4]]), "]")
}
fmt_paired <- \(tt) paste0("[t(", tt$parameter, ") = ", formatC(tt$statistic, format = "f", digits = 3), ", p ", fmt_p(tt$p.value), "]")
```

```{r}
boreal_zones <- c("Ba", "Bb", "BM")
temperate_zones <- c("TeDc", "TeDo", "TeM")
grassland_zones <- c("TeBSk", "TeBWk")
zone_names <- c("Ba", "Bb", "BM", "P", "TeBSk", "TeBWk", "TeDc", "TeDo", "TeM")
zone_codes <- stats::setNames(seq_along(zone_names), zone_names)
row_of <- function(zone, type, season) dplyr::case_when(
  zone %in% boreal_zones & type == "Crown" ~ "Boreal forest, Crown fire",
  zone %in% boreal_zones & type == "Surface" ~ "Boreal forest, Surface fire",
  zone %in% boreal_zones ~ "Boreal forest, Wildfire (general)",
  zone %in% temperate_zones ~ "Other temperate forests, Wildfire",
  zone %in% grassland_zones & season %in% c("April to May", "June") ~ "Savanna grasslands and pastures, All savanna grasslands (early dry season burns)",
  zone %in% grassland_zones ~ "Savanna grasslands and pastures, Grassland (mid or late dry season burns)",
  zone == "P" ~ "Other vegetation types, Tundra")
```

```{r}
#| label: inventory
#| output: false
# ECCC National Inventory Report 1990-2024, Tables 6-1 and 6-5
# https://data-donnees.az.ec.gc.ca/data/substances/monitor/canada-s-official-greenhouse-gas-inventory/E-LULUCF/?lang=en
eccc_table <- function(table, file) fetch(paste0("https://data-donnees.az.ec.gc.ca/api/file?path=",
  URLencode(paste0("/substances/monitor/canada-s-official-greenhouse-gas-inventory/E-LULUCF/NIR2026_Table ", table, "_All_Years_PTs.xlsx"), reserved = TRUE)), file)
eccc_files <- c(accounts = "02.inputs/eccc/lulucf-2026.csv", Canada = "02.inputs/eccc/lulucf-2026-categories.csv", BC = "02.inputs/eccc/lulucf-2026-categories-bc.csv")
if (!all(file.exists(eccc_files))) {
  eccc_table("6-1", "02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-1.xlsx")
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets("02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-1.xlsx")
  long <- c(Canada = "NATIONAL$", BC = " BC$") |>
    purrr::map(\(s) readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-1.xlsx", sheet = grep(s, sheets, value = TRUE), skip = 3, col_types = "text", .name_repair = "unique_quiet") |>
      dplyr::transmute(category = dplyr::case_when(grepl("TOTAL", ...1) ~ "Sector total", grepl("^Natural disturbances", ...2) ~ "Natural disturbances", grepl("^[a-g]\\.$", ...1) ~ ...2),
        dplyr::across(dplyr::matches("^[0-9]{4}$"), as.numeric)) |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(category)) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(-category, names_to = "year", values_to = "kt", names_transform = as.integer)) |>
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "region")
  for (r in c("Canada", "BC")) readr::write_csv(dplyr::select(dplyr::filter(long, region == r), -region), eccc_files[[r]], na = "")
  long |>
    dplyr::filter(category %in% c("Sector total", "Natural disturbances")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(region, component = dplyr::if_else(category == "Sector total", "human", "natural"), year, mt = kt / 1000) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = mt) |>
    readr::write_csv(eccc_files[["accounts"]])
}
eccc <- readr::read_csv(eccc_files[["accounts"]], show_col_types = FALSE) |> dplyr::mutate(net = human + natural)
stopifnot(nrow(eccc) == 2 * 35, !anyNA(eccc))
national <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "Canada")
province <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "BC")
category_levels <- c("Forest Land", "Cropland", "Grassland", "Wetlands", "Settlements", "Harvested Wood Products", "Sector total", "Natural disturbances")
categories <- readr::read_csv(eccc_files[["Canada"]], show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(kt)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(mt = kt / 1000, category = factor(category, levels = category_levels),
    panel = factor(dplyr::if_else(category == "Natural disturbances", "Natural disturbances, shown beside the total and left out of it", "Reported categories and their total"),
      levels = c("Reported categories and their total", "Natural disturbances, shown beside the total and left out of it")))
categories_bc <- readr::read_csv(eccc_files[["BC"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/eccc/natural-components-2026.csv")) {
  eccc_table("6-5", "02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-5.xlsx")
  readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/eccc/raw/table-6-5.xlsx", sheet = "Table 6-5 NATIONAL", skip = 2, col_types = "text", .name_repair = "unique_quiet") |>
    dplyr::transmute(component = dplyr::case_when(grepl("^Areas with natural", ...2) ~ "area_kha", grepl("^Emissions/removals from lands impacted", ...2) ~ "line",
      grepl("^Wildfires – direct", ...2) ~ "direct", grepl("^Wildfires – indirect", ...2) ~ "indirect",
      grepl("^Post-wildfire", ...2) ~ "post_fire", grepl("^Insects", ...2) ~ "insects", grepl("^Other natural", ...2) ~ "other"),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::matches("^[0-9]{4}$"), \(x) dplyr::coalesce(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)), 0))) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(component)) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-component, names_to = "year", values_to = "value", names_transform = as.integer) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = value) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/eccc/natural-components-2026.csv")
}
cbm <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/eccc/natural-components-2026.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-c(year, area_kha), \(x) x / 1000), immediate = direct + indirect)
stopifnot(identical(cbm$year, national$year), max(abs(cbm$line - national$natural)) < 0.5)
```

```{r}
#| label: faostat
#| output: false
# FAOSTAT Emissions from Fires (GI)
# https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/GI
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv") && nzchar(Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_USER")) && nzchar(Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_PASSWORD"))) {
  login <- httr2::request("https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/auth/login") |>
    httr2::req_body_form(username = Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_USER"), password = Sys.getenv("FAOSTAT_PASSWORD")) |>
    httr2::req_perform() |>
    httr2::resp_body_json()
  httr2::request("https://faostatservices.fao.org/api/v1/en/data/GI") |>
    httr2::req_url_query(area = "33", area_cs = "FAO", output_type = "csv") |>
    httr2::req_auth_bearer_token(login$AuthenticationResult$AccessToken) |>
    httr2::req_perform(path = "02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv")
}
fires <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/canada-fires.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::select(item = Item, element = Element, year = Year, source = Source, value = Value, unit = Unit, flag = Flag)
forest <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(item == "Forest fires", source == "FAO TIER 1", element %in% c("Burned Area", "Emissions (CO2)", "Emissions (CH4)"), year >= 2001) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::rename(Year = year, `Burned area (ha)` = `Burned Area`, `CO2 (kt)` = `Emissions (CO2)`, `CH4 (kt)` = `Emissions (CH4)`)
used <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, item %in% c("Other forest", "Woody savanna", "Savanna", "Grassland", "Open shrubland", "Closed shrubland")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(element = dplyr::case_match(element, "Burned Area" ~ "ha", "Emissions (CO2)" ~ "co2", "Emissions (CH4)" ~ "ch4", "Emissions (N2O)" ~ "n2o", .default = "dm")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(item, year), names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(ha > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fuel = dm / ha, dplyr::across(c(co2, ch4, n2o), \(x) x * 1e6 / dm))
coefficients <- used |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = item, years = dplyr::n(), ha = sum(ha) / 24, fuel_min = min(fuel), fuel_max = max(fuel), co2 = mean(co2), ch4 = mean(ch4), n2o = mean(n2o)) |>
  dplyr::filter(years == 24) |>
  dplyr::arrange(item != "Other forest", -ha) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Item = item, `Burned area (ha a year)` = format(round(ha), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
    `Fuel (t/ha)` = dplyr::if_else(round(fuel_min, 1) == round(fuel_max, 1), sprintf("%.1f", fuel_min), sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", fuel_min, fuel_max)),
    `IPCC biomass consumption row` = dplyr::coalesce(table_2_4$`IPCC biomass consumption row`[match(round(fuel_min, 1), table_2_4$fuel)], "Between all boreal forest and all other temperate forests"),
    `CH4 (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.1f", ch4), `N2O (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.2f", n2o), `CO2 (g/kg)` = dplyr::if_else(is.na(co2), "", format(round(co2), big.mark = ","))) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(Item = "Emission factor row, extra tropical forest", `Burned area (ha a year)` = "", `Fuel (t/ha)` = "", `IPCC biomass consumption row` = "",
    `CH4 (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.1f", table_2_5$ch4[2]), `N2O (g/kg)` = sprintf("%.2f", table_2_5$n2o[2]), `CO2 (g/kg)` = format(table_2_5$co2[2], big.mark = ",")))
savanna_share <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, element == "Burned Area", item %in% c("Forest fires", "Savanna fires")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = item, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = 100 * `Savanna fires` / (`Savanna fires` + `Forest fires`))
co2_2023 <- forest[["CO2 (kt)"]][forest$Year == 2023] / 1000
burn_2023 <- used[used$item == "Other forest" & used$year == 2023, ]
u_fuel <- u_term(table_2_4$se[1:2], table_2_4$fuel[1:2])
u_ef <- u_term(table_2_5$co2_sd[1], table_2_5$co2[1])
u_forest <- sqrt(u_fuel^2 + u_ef^2)
# FAOSTAT Emissions from Fires (GI), AllFires_OrganicSoils
# https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/GI
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/faostat/organic-soil-fires.csv")) {
  flat <- gsub("[\n ]+", " ", paste(pdftools::pdf_text("02.inputs/faostat/raw/AllFires_OrganicSoils.pdf"), collapse = "\n"))
  rx <- "[0-9]+,(?:\"[^\"]*\"|[^,]*),6993,Fires in organic soils,(?:CH4 emissions|CO2 emissions|Burned Area|Biomass burned [(]dry matter[)]),[0-9]{4},[0-9.eE+-]+,(?:ha|tonnes|kilotonnes)"
  readr::write_lines(c("area_code,area,item_code,item,element,year,value,unit", regmatches(flat, gregexpr(rx, flat))[[1]]), "02.inputs/faostat/organic-soil-fires.csv")
}
peat <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/faostat/organic-soil-fires.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(peat) == dplyr::n_distinct(peat$area) * dplyr::n_distinct(peat$year) * 4)
canada <- peat |>
  dplyr::filter(area == "Canada", element %in% c("Burned Area", "CO2 emissions", "CH4 emissions")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = year, names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::rename(Year = year, `Burned area (ha)` = `Burned Area`, `CO2 (kt)` = `CO2 emissions`, `CH4 (kt)` = `CH4 emissions`)
```

```{r}
#| label: layers

# FAO Global Ecological Zones (GEZ 2010)
# https://data.apps.fao.org/catalog/dataset/2fb209d0-fd34-4e5e-a3d8-a13c241eb61b
fetch("https://storage.googleapis.com/fao-maps-catalog-data/uuid/2fb209d0-fd34-4e5e-a3d8-a13c241eb61b/resources/gez2010.zip", "02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez2010.zip")
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
canada_outline <- sf::st_make_valid(rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = 50, country = "Canada", returnclass = "sf")["name"])
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez-canada.gpkg")) {
  sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez2010.zip"), "/gez_2010_wgs84.shp"), quiet = TRUE) |>
    sf::st_make_valid() |>
    sf::st_intersection(canada_outline) |>
    sf::st_transform(3978) |>
    sf::st_write("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez-canada.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)
}
gez <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/gez-canada.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) |> dplyr::filter(gez_abbrev != "Water")
gez$mha <- as.numeric(sf::st_area(gez)) / 1e10
bc_outline <- rnaturalearth::ne_states(country = "Canada", returnclass = "sf") |> dplyr::filter(name == "British Columbia") |> dplyr::select(name) |> sf::st_transform(3978)
# IPCC default soil classes (Batjes 2010), no retrieval link, see 02.inputs/README.md
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ipcc/soil-type-canada.tif"))
  terra::crop(terra::rast("02.inputs/ipcc/raw/soil_type.tif"), terra::ext(-141.5, -52, 41, 84)) |>
    terra::writeRaster("02.inputs/ipcc/soil-type-canada.tif", datatype = "INT1U", gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE")

cover_of <- function(code) dplyr::case_when(code %in% 1:5 ~ cover_labels[1], code %in% 6:7 ~ cover_labels[2], code == 8 ~ cover_labels[3],
  code == 9 ~ cover_labels[4], code == 10 ~ cover_labels[5], code == 11 ~ cover_labels[6], .default = cover_labels[7])
# Managed boreal forest and boreal extent, Natural Resources Canada

fetch("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/fuels/current/FBP_FuelTypes_Canada_2026_250m.tiff", "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/FBP_FuelTypes_Canada_2026_250m.tiff")

grid <- terra::rast(terra::ext(sf::st_bbox(gez)), resolution = 2000, crs = "EPSG:3978")
on_grid <- \(r) terra::values(terra::project(r, grid, method = "near"))[, 1]
zone_r <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(gez), grid, field = "gez_abbrev")
zone_code <- terra::levels(zone_r)[[1]]$gez_abbrev[match(terra::values(zone_r)[, 1], terra::levels(zone_r)[[1]]$ID)]

}
category <- dplyr::case_when(is.na(zone_code) ~ NA_character_, cover_code %in% c(1:5, 8, 9) ~ "Forest", cover_code %in% 6:7 ~ "Shrubland",

fuel <- dplyr::case_when(category == "Forest" & zone_code %in% c(boreal_zones, "P") ~ 52.8, category == "Forest" ~ 19.8, category == "Shrubland" ~ 14.3,
```

```{r}
#| label: burned-area

# NBAC summary statistics, version 2026-05-13
# https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/
fetch("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx")
nbac <- readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/NBAC_summarystats_1972_to_2025_20260513.xlsx", sheet = "sumstats_admin_name", skip = 2) |>
  dplyr::transmute(year = as.integer(YEAR), ha = as.numeric(CANADA)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(year))
nbac_2023 <- nbac$ha[nbac$year == 2023]
# National Burned Area Composite (NBAC), fire perimeters
# https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/nbac/nbac-keyed-1972-2024.csv")) {
  grid_250 <- terra::rast(terra::ext(terra::vect(gez)), resolution = 250, crs = "EPSG:3978")
  key_250 <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(dplyr::mutate(gez, code = unname(zone_codes[gez_abbrev]))), grid_250, field = "code", background = 0) +
    10 * terra::classify(terra::project(soil == 1, grid_250, method = "near"), cbind(NA, 0)) +
    100 * terra::rasterize(terra::vect(boreal_map("Managed_Boreal_Forest")), grid_250, field = 1, background = 0) +
    1000 * terra::rasterize(terra::vect(boreal_map("Boreal_Forest")), grid_250, field = 1, background = 0)
  dir.create("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/nbac", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  dir.create("02.inputs/nbac", showWarnings = FALSE)
  key_250 <- terra::writeRaster(key_250, "02.inputs/nrcan/raw/nbac/key-250m.tif", datatype = "INT2U", overwrite = TRUE, gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE")
  purrr::map(1972:2024, function(y) {
    zip <- sprintf("02.inputs/nrcan/raw/nbac/NBAC_%d_20260513.zip", y)
    fetch(paste0("https://cwfis.cfs.nrcan.gc.ca/downloads/nbac/", basename(zip)), zip)
    layer <- sub("\\.zip$", "", basename(zip))
    perimeters <- sf::st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", normalizePath(zip), "/", layer, ".shp"), quiet = TRUE,
      query = paste0('SELECT BASRC, FIREMAPS, POLY_HA, ADJ_HA, ADJ_FLAG, PRESCRIBED FROM "', layer, '"')) |>
      dplyr::filter(!PRESCRIBED %in% "true") |>
      sf::st_zm() |>
      sf::st_transform(3978)
    cells <- exactextractr::exact_extract(key_250, perimeters, progress = FALSE)
    purrr::imap(cells, \(d, i) dplyr::summarise(d, w = sum(coverage_fraction), .by = value) |> dplyr::mutate(id = i)) |>
      purrr::list_rbind() |>
      dplyr::mutate(w = w / sum(w), .by = id) |>
      dplyr::left_join(dplyr::mutate(sf::st_drop_geometry(perimeters), id = dplyr::row_number()), by = "id") |>
      dplyr::summarise(ha_mapped = sum(w * POLY_HA), ha = sum(w * dplyr::coalesce(ADJ_HA, POLY_HA)), .by = c(value, BASRC, FIREMAPS, ADJ_FLAG)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(year = y, .before = 1)
  }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind() |>
    dplyr::transmute(year, zone_code = value %% 10L, organic = (value %/% 10L) %% 10L, in_managed = (value %/% 100L) %% 10L, in_boreal = value %/% 1000L,
      source = BASRC, map_source = FIREMAPS, adjusted = ADJ_FLAG %in% "true", ha_mapped, ha) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/nbac/nbac-keyed-1972-2024.csv")
}
nbac_keyed <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/nbac/nbac-keyed-1972-2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

to_geojson <- function(x, name) {
  path <- paste0("02.inputs/ee/raw/ee-", name, ".geojson")
  if (file.exists(path)) return(path)
  dir.create("02.inputs/ee/raw", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  x <- x |> sf::st_make_valid() |> sf::st_simplify(dTolerance = 2000) |> sf::st_make_valid() |> sf::st_transform(4326)
  sf::st_write(x[!sf::st_is_empty(x), ], path, quiet = TRUE)
  path
}
ee_boundaries <- function() {
  if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ee/raw/ee-organic.geojson")) {
    organic_cells <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(soil == 1, dissolve = TRUE))
    dir.create("02.inputs/ee/raw", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    sf::st_write(sf::st_set_crs(sf::st_make_valid(organic_cells[organic_cells[[1]] == 1, 1]), 4326), "02.inputs/ee/raw/ee-organic.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
  }
  py <- reticulate::import_main()
  py$ZONES <- to_geojson(gez |> dplyr::mutate(code = unname(zone_codes[gez_abbrev])) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(code)) |> dplyr::group_by(code) |> dplyr::summarise(.groups = "drop"), "zones")
  py$MANAGED <- to_geojson(boreal_map("Managed_Boreal_Forest") |> dplyr::summarise(), "managed")
  py$BOREAL <- to_geojson(boreal_map("Boreal_Forest") |> dplyr::summarise(), "boreal")
  py$ORGANIC <- "02.inputs/ee/raw/ee-organic.geojson"
  py$UNC_MAX <- 20L
  py
}
ee_py <- r"(
import ee, json, csv, os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
ee.Initialize(project='manuscripts-personal')
def fc(path, prop=None):
    return ee.FeatureCollection([ee.Feature(ee.Geometry(f['geometry'], 'EPSG:4326', False), {prop: f['properties'][prop]} if prop else {}) for f in json.load(open(path))['features']])
paint = lambda c, v=1: ee.Image().byte().paint(c, v).unmask(0)
)"
# MODIS burned area, MCD64A1 v6.1
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD64A1.061
# MODIS land cover, MCD12Q1 v6.1
# https://doi.org/10.5067/MODIS/MCD12Q1.061
# FAO GAUL 2015 country boundary
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/FAO_GAUL_2015_level0
mcd64a1_py <- r"(
canada_mask = ee.Image().byte().paint(ee.FeatureCollection('FAO/GAUL/2015/level0').filter(ee.Filter.eq('ADM0_NAME', 'Canada')), 1)
modis = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD12Q1').first().select('LC_Type1').projection()
scale = 463.3127165275
pixel_ha = scale * scale / 1e4
def lc_year(year):
    return {2023: 2022, 2024: 2023}.get(year, year)
def burned_cover(year):
    monthly = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD64A1').filterDate(f'{year}-01-01', f'{year + 1}-01-01')
    burned = monthly.map(lambda i: i.select('BurnDate').gt(0).And(i.select('Uncertainty').lt(UNC_MAX))).max()
    cover = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MCD12Q1').filterDate(f'{lc_year(year)}-01-01', f'{lc_year(year) + 1}-01-01').first().select('LC_Type1')
    return burned, cover
def tile_counts(stack, tiles):
    os.makedirs(tiles, exist_ok=True)
    lons = [-141.5 + i * 7.5 for i in range(13)]
    lats = [41 + j * 5.4 for j in range(9)]
    boxes = [(f'b{i:02d}{j:02d}', ee.Geometry.Rectangle([lons[i], lats[j], lons[i + 1], lats[j + 1]], 'EPSG:4326', False)) for i in range(12) for j in range(8)]
    def run_box(name, box, depth=0):
        path = f'{tiles}/{name}.json'
        if os.path.exists(path):
            return name
        try:
            hist = stack.reduceRegion(reducer=ee.Reducer.frequencyHistogram(), geometry=box, crs=modis, scale=scale, maxPixels=1e11).getInfo()
        except Exception as e:
            if depth >= 2 or 'time' not in str(e).lower():
                raise
            c = box.coordinates().getInfo()[0]
            x0, y0 = c[0]; x1, y1 = c[2]; xm, ym = (x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2
            hist = {}
            for k, (p, q, r, s) in enumerate(((x0, y0, xm, ym), (xm, y0, x1, ym), (x0, ym, xm, y1), (xm, ym, x1, y1))):
                run_box(f'{name}_{k}', ee.Geometry.Rectangle([p, q, r, s], 'EPSG:4326', False), depth + 1)
                for band, h in json.load(open(f'{tiles}/{name}_{k}.json')).items():
                    for key, n in (h or {}).items():
                        hist.setdefault(band, {})
                        hist[band][key] = hist[band].get(key, 0) + n
        json.dump(hist, open(path, 'w'))
        return name
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool:
        for done in as_completed([pool.submit(run_box, name, box) for name, box in boxes]):
            done.result()
    counts = {}
    for name, _ in boxes:
        for band, h in json.load(open(f'{tiles}/{name}.json')).items():
            for key, n in (h or {}).items():
                counts[(int(band[1:]), int(float(key)))] = counts.get((int(band[1:]), int(float(key))), 0) + n
    return counts
)"

# Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 surface reflectance
# https://doi.org/10.5066/P9IAXOVV and https://doi.org/10.5066/P9OGBGM6
# JRC Global Surface Water v1.4
# https://doi.org/10.1038/nature20584
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/landsat/landsat-keyed-1985-2024.csv")) {
  py <- ee_boundaries()
  py$SEEDS <- "02.inputs/landsat/raw/seeds-1972-2025.csv"
  py$OUTDIR <- "02.inputs/landsat/raw"
  py$Y0 <- 1985L
  py$Y1 <- 2024L
  reticulate::py_run_string(paste0(ee_py, r"(
import datetime as dt
ee.data.setDeadline(300000)
THRESHOLD, SCALE = 0.12, 30
# Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 surface reflectance, https://doi.org/10.5066/P9IAXOVV and https://doi.org/10.5066/P9OGBGM6
SR = [('LANDSAT/LT04/C02/T1_L2', 'SR_B3', 'SR_B4'), ('LANDSAT/LT05/C02/T1_L2', 'SR_B3', 'SR_B4'), ('LANDSAT/LE07/C02/T1_L2', 'SR_B3', 'SR_B4'),
      ('LANDSAT/LC08/C02/T1_L2', 'SR_B4', 'SR_B5'), ('LANDSAT/LC09/C02/T1_L2', 'SR_B4', 'SR_B5')]
# JRC Global Surface Water v1.4, https://doi.org/10.1038/nature20584
water = ee.Image('JRC/GSW1_4/GlobalSurfaceWater').select('occurrence').gte(50).unmask(0)
P3978 = ee.Projection('EPSG:3978').atScale(SCALE)
key = paint(fc(ZONES, 'code'), 'code').add(paint(fc(ORGANIC)).multiply(10)).add(paint(fc(MANAGED)).multiply(100)).add(paint(fc(BOREAL)).multiply(1000)).toInt16().rename('key')

def sr_prep(img, red, nir):
    bad = img.select('QA_PIXEL').bitwiseAnd(0b111110).neq(0)
    return img.select([red, nir], ['red', 'nir']).multiply(0.0000275).add(-0.2).updateMask(bad.Not())

def scenes(start, end, geom):
    col = None
    for cid, red, nir in SR:
        c = ee.ImageCollection(cid).filterBounds(geom).filterDate(start, end).filter(ee.Filter.lte('CLOUD_COVER', 80)).map(lambda i, r=red, n=nir: sr_prep(i, r, n))
        col = c if col is None else col.merge(c)
    return col

def windows(row):
    y = int(row['year'])
    rep = dt.date.fromisoformat(row['rep_date']) if row['rep_date'][:2] in ('19', '20') else dt.date(y, 6, 1)
    out = dt.date.fromisoformat(row['out_date']) if row['out_date'][:2] in ('19', '20') else dt.date(y, 8, 1)
    out = max(out, rep)
    start = out + dt.timedelta(days=1)
    end = min(start + dt.timedelta(days=60), dt.date(y, 9, 30))
    late = (end - start).days < 15
    if late:
        start, end = dt.date(y + 1, 6, 1), dt.date(y + 1, 9, 30)
        pre = (dt.date(y - 1, 6, 1), dt.date(y - 1, 9, 30))
    else:
        pre = (start.replace(year=start.year - 1), end.replace(year=end.year - 1))
    fallback = ((dt.date(y - 1, 6, 1), dt.date(y - 1, 9, 30)), (dt.date(y + 1, 6, 1), dt.date(y + 1, 9, 30)))
    return [(pre[0].isoformat(), pre[1].isoformat()), (start.isoformat(), end.isoformat())], late, [tuple(d.isoformat() for d in w) for w in fallback]

def run(row, owner, idx):
    r = (float(row['size_ha']) * 1e4 / 3.141592653589793) ** 0.5
    pt = ee.Geometry.Point([float(row['lon']), float(row['lat'])])
    extent = pt.buffer(r + 5000, 10).bounds(10, 'EPSG:3978')
    frame = extent.buffer(180, 10).difference(extent, 10)
    (w_pre, w_post), late, (f_pre, f_post) = windows(row)
    region = extent.buffer(500)
    def composite(w, f):
        a = scenes(w[0], w[1], region); b = scenes(f[0], f[1], region)
        col = ee.ImageCollection(ee.Algorithms.If(a.size().gt(0), a, b))
        return col.median().normalizedDifference(['nir', 'red']).rename('v').reproject(P3978), a.size()
    pre, n_pre = composite(w_pre, f_pre)
    post, n_post = composite(w_post, f_post)
    diff = pre.subtract(post)
    m = diff.reduceRegion(ee.Reducer.mean(), frame, SCALE, 'EPSG:3978', None, False, 1e9).get('v')
    off = ee.Number(ee.Algorithms.If(m, m, 0))
    rd = diff.subtract(off).divide(pre.abs().sqrt().max(0.05)).updateMask(water.Not())
    mine = owner.eq(idx)
    burned = rd.gt(THRESHOLD).And(mine)
    area = ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(1e4)
    grouped = area.updateMask(burned).addBands(key).reduceRegion(ee.Reducer.sum().group(1, 'key'), extent, SCALE, 'EPSG:3978', None, False, 1e10)
    valid = area.updateMask(rd.mask().And(mine)).reduceRegion(ee.Reducer.sum(), extent, SCALE, 'EPSG:3978', None, False, 1e10)
    owned = area.updateMask(mine).reduceRegion(ee.Reducer.sum(), extent, SCALE, 'EPSG:3978', None, False, 1e10)
    res = ee.Dictionary({'groups': grouped.get('groups'), 'valid_ha': valid.get('area'), 'owned_ha': owned.get('area'), 'off': off,
                         'n_pre': n_pre, 'n_post': n_post}).getInfo()
    res.update({'year': int(row['year']), 'agency': row['agency'], 'fire_id': row['fire_id'], 'size_ha': float(row['size_ha']),
                'lon': float(row['lon']), 'lat': float(row['lat']), 'late': late, 'pre': '/'.join(w_pre), 'post': '/'.join(w_post)})
    return res

all_rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(SEEDS)))
os.makedirs(OUTDIR, exist_ok=True)
for attempt in range(3):
    for year in range(Y0, Y1 + 1):
        out = os.path.join(OUTDIR, f'landsat-{year}.json')
        rows = sorted([r for r in all_rows if int(r['year']) == year], key=lambda r: float(r['size_ha']))
        feats = []
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            r = (float(row['size_ha']) * 1e4 / 3.141592653589793) ** 0.5
            feats.append(ee.Feature(ee.Geometry.Point([float(row['lon']), float(row['lat'])]).buffer(r + 5000, 10).bounds(10, 'EPSG:3978'), {'idx': i + 1}))
        owner = ee.Image().int().paint(ee.FeatureCollection(feats), 'idx').unmask(0).reproject(P3978)
        done = {}
        if os.path.exists(out):
            done = {d['i']: d for d in json.load(open(out)) if 'error' not in d}
        todo = [(i, row) for i, row in enumerate(rows) if i + 1 not in done]
        print(year, len(rows), 'fires', len(todo), 'to do', flush=True)
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
            futs = {pool.submit(run, row, owner, i + 1): (i, row) for i, row in todo}
            for k, f in enumerate(as_completed(futs)):
                i, row = futs[f]
                try:
                    d = f.result()
                except Exception as e:
                    d = {'year': year, 'agency': row['agency'], 'fire_id': row['fire_id'], 'size_ha': float(row['size_ha']), 'error': str(e)[:300]}
                d['i'] = i + 1
                done[i + 1] = d
                if k % 50 == 0:
                    json.dump(list(done.values()), open(out, 'w'))
        json.dump(list(done.values()), open(out, 'w'))
        print(year, 'done', sum('error' in d for d in done.values()), 'errors', flush=True)
print('ALL DONE', flush=True)
)"))
  purrr::map(1985:2024, function(y) {
    results <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sprintf("02.inputs/landsat/raw/landsat-%d.json", y), simplifyVector = FALSE)
    failed <- vapply(results, \(f) !is.null(f$error), TRUE)
    purrr::map(results[!failed], \(f) tibble::tibble(key = vapply(f$groups, \(g) as.integer(g$key), 0L), ha = vapply(f$groups, \(g) g$sum, 0))) |>
      purrr::list_rbind() |>
      dplyr::summarise(ha = sum(ha), .by = key) |>
      dplyr::mutate(year = y, fires = length(results), failed = sum(failed), .before = 1)
  }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind() |>
    dplyr::transmute(year, fires, failed, zone_code = key %% 10L, organic = (key %/% 10L) %% 10L, in_managed = (key %/% 100L) %% 10L, in_boreal = key %/% 1000L, ha) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/landsat/landsat-keyed-1985-2024.csv")
}
landsat_keyed <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/landsat/landsat-keyed-1985-2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tier1-lines
#| output: false
tier1_line <- function(cohorts, first) {
  burned <- cohorts |>
    dplyr::filter(ha > 0) |>
    dplyr::mutate(row = row_of(gez_abbrev, type, season)) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(rows_2_4[, c("row", "mb_cf", "ef_row")], by = "row") |>
    dplyr::inner_join(table_2_5, by = "ef_row") |>
    dplyr::inner_join(biomass_4_7, by = "gez_abbrev") |>
    dplyr::mutate(dm_mt = ha * mb_cf / 1e6, peat_mt = dplyr::if_else(soil == "Organic", ha * peat_fuel[["mean"]] / 1e6, 0),
      co2_mt = (dm_mt * co2 + peat_mt * peat_ef$co2) / 1e3, co2e_mt = co2_mt + ((dm_mt * ch4 + peat_mt * peat_ef$ch4) * 28 + dm_mt * n2o * 265) / 1e3,
      killed_mt = ha * pmax(bw - mb_cf, 0) * 0.47 * 44 / 12 / 1e6)
  regrowth <- burned |>
    dplyr::mutate(balance = (co2_mt + killed_mt) * 1e6 / ha) |>
    dplyr::cross_join(tibble::tibble(t = (first + 1):2024)) |>
    dplyr::filter(t > year) |>
    dplyr::mutate(age = t - year, removed_mt = ha * (pmin(cumulative_removal(gez_abbrev, age), balance) - pmin(cumulative_removal(gez_abbrev, age - 1), balance)) / 1e6)
  tibble::tibble(year = first:2024) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::summarise(burned, ha = sum(ha), immediate = sum(co2e_mt), killed = sum(killed_mt), .by = year), by = "year") |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::rename(dplyr::summarise(regrowth, post_fire = -sum(removed_mt), .by = t), year = t), by = "year") |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(ha, immediate, killed, post_fire), \(x) dplyr::coalesce(x, 0))) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cbm[, c("year", "insects", "other")], by = "year") |>
    dplyr::mutate(fire = immediate + killed + post_fire, line = fire + insects + other)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: treatments
#| output: false
background_level <- function(x) {
  repeat {
    outlier <- x > mean(x) + 2 * stats::sd(x)
    if (!any(outlier)) return(c(level = mean(x), margin = 2 * stats::sd(x)))
    x <- x[!outlier]
  }
}
in_window <- function(years, n) years >= 2017 - n & years <= 2016
reduce <- function(account, years) round(mean(account[years %in% 2012:2016]) - account, 1)[years %in% 2017:2024]
treat <- function(human, nd, years, test, test_years, n, method) {
  now <- test[match(years, test_years)]
  base <- test[in_window(test_years, n)]
  counted <- switch(method,
    none = nd,
    canada = 0 * nd,
    threshold = ifelse(now > mean(base) + 2 * stats::sd(base), 0, nd),
    kyoto_line = {
      b <- background_level(nd[in_window(years, n)])
      ifelse(nd > b[["level"]] + b[["margin"]], b[["level"]], nd)
    },
    kyoto_area = {
      b <- background_level(base)
      ifelse(now > b[["level"]] + b[["margin"]], nd * b[["level"]] / now, nd)
  })
  list(reductions = reduce(human + counted, years), excluded = sum((nd - counted)[years %in% 2017:2024]))
}
treatment_names <- c(none = "No disaggregation", canada = "Canada's approach", threshold = "Threshold rule", kyoto_line = "Background level", kyoto_area = "Background level")
tested <- c("threshold", "kyoto_line", "kyoto_area")
kyoto_bl <- purrr::map(c(13, 20, 27), \(n) background_level(national$natural[in_window(national$year, n)])) |> stats::setNames(c(13, 20, 27))
line_runs <- function(first) dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(method = c("none", "canada"), series = c("none", "canada"), n = 13),
  tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", series = "Fire emissions", n = 13:(2017 - first[["fire"]])),
  tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", series = "Natural disturbance line", n = 13:(2017 - first[["line"]])),
  tibble::tibble(method = "threshold", series = "Burned area", n = 13:(2017 - first[["area"]])),
  tibble::tibble(method = "kyoto_line", series = "Natural disturbance line", n = 13:(2017 - first[["line"]])),
  tibble::tibble(method = "kyoto_area", series = "Burned area", n = 13:(2017 - first[["area"]])))
line_series <- function(l, area) {
  ok <- !is.na(l$line)
  list(nd = l$line[ok], years = l$year[ok], human = national$human[match(l$year[ok], national$year)],
    tests = list(none = list(l$line[ok], l$year[ok]), canada = list(l$line[ok], l$year[ok]), `Fire emissions` = list(l$immediate + l$killed, l$year),
      `Natural disturbance line` = list(l$line[ok], l$year[ok]), `Burned area` = list(area$ha, area$year)),
    first = c(fire = min(l$year), line = min(l$year[ok]), area = min(area$year)), area = area)
}
series_of <- list(MODIS = line_series(tier1_lines$MODIS, tier1_lines$MODIS[, c("year", "ha")]), NBAC = line_series(tier1_lines$NBAC, tier1_lines$NBAC[, c("year", "ha")]),
  Canada = line_series(tier1_lines$Canada, tier1_lines$NBAC[, c("year", "ha")]))
observed_lines <- purrr::imap(series_of, function(s, estimate) purrr::pmap(line_runs(s$first), function(method, series, n) {
  out <- treat(s$human, s$nd, s$years, s$tests[[series]][[1]], s$tests[[series]][[2]], n, method)
  tibble::tibble(estimate, method, series, n, positive = sum(out$reductions[out$reductions > 0]), years_positive = sum(out$reductions > 0), net = sum(out$reductions), excluded = out$excluded)
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()) |> purrr::list_rbind()
simulate_line <- function(s, year_term = TRUE, area_trend = TRUE, histories = 2000, seed = 2026) {
  set.seed(seed)
  fit_a <- stats::lm(log(ha) ~ year, s$area)
  fit_l <- stats::lm(nd ~ I(ha / 1e6) + year, data.frame(nd = s$nd, year = s$years, ha = s$area$ha[match(s$years, s$area$year)]))
  runs <- dplyr::filter(line_runs(s$first), series %in% c("none", "canada", "Burned area") | method == "kyoto_line")
  human <- rep(mean(national$human[national$year %in% 2012:2016]), length(s$years))
  area_fit <- if (area_trend) stats::fitted(fit_a) else rep(mean(stats::fitted(fit_a)), nrow(s$area))
  line_year <- if (year_term) s$years else rep(2014, length(s$years))
  draws <- replicate(histories, {
    ha <- exp(area_fit + sample(stats::residuals(fit_a), replace = TRUE))
    nd <- stats::predict(fit_l, data.frame(ha = ha[match(s$years, s$area$year)], year = line_year)) + sample(stats::residuals(fit_l), replace = TRUE)
    unlist(purrr::pmap(runs[, c("method", "n")], function(method, n) treat(human, nd, s$years, ha, s$area$year, n, method)$reductions))
  })
  means <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(i) colMeans(draws[(i - 1) * 8 + 1:8, , drop = FALSE]), numeric(histories)))
  summary <- purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(i) {
    x <- as.vector(draws[(i - 1) * 8 + 1:8, ])
    ci <- ci95(means[i, ])
    tibble::tibble(runs[i, ], bias = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), ci_low = ci[1], ci_high = ci[2], half_width = unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.95) - stats::quantile(x, 0.05)) / 2)
  }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
  list(summary = summary, means = means, runs = runs, fit_area = fit_a, fit_line = fit_l)
}
sims <- purrr::map(series_of, simulate_line)
simulated_lines <- purrr::imap(sims, \(x, estimate) dplyr::mutate(x$summary, estimate, .before = 1)) |> purrr::list_rbind()
lines_sensitivity <- purrr::imap(series_of, function(s, estimate) dplyr::bind_rows(
  no_year_term = simulate_line(s, year_term = FALSE)$summary, no_trend = simulate_line(s, year_term = FALSE, area_trend = FALSE)$summary, .id = "check") |>
  dplyr::mutate(estimate, .before = 1)) |> purrr::list_rbind()
rm_anova_of <- function(y) {
  k <- nrow(y)
  h <- ncol(y)
  g <- mean(y)
  ss_t <- h * sum((rowMeans(y) - g)^2)
  ss_e <- sum((y - g)^2) - ss_t - k * sum((colMeans(y) - g)^2)
  f <- (ss_t / (k - 1)) / (ss_e / ((k - 1) * (h - 1)))
  tibble::tibble(df1 = k - 1, df2 = (k - 1) * (h - 1), F = f, p = stats::pf(f, k - 1, (k - 1) * (h - 1), lower.tail = FALSE))
}
lines_tests <- purrr::imap(sims, function(x, estimate) dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(test = "treatments", rm_anova_of(x$means[x$runs$n == 13, , drop = FALSE])),
  purrr::map(tested, \(m) tibble::tibble(test = m, rm_anova_of(x$means[x$runs$method == m, , drop = FALSE]))) |> purrr::list_rbind()) |>
  dplyr::mutate(estimate, .before = 1)) |> purrr::list_rbind()
lines_shift <- purrr::imap(sims, function(x, estimate) purrr::map(tested, function(m) {
  rows <- which(x$runs$method == m)
  d <- x$means[rows[which.max(x$runs$n[rows])], ] - x$means[rows[which.min(x$runs$n[rows])], ]
  tibble::tibble(estimate, method = m, longest = max(x$runs$n[rows]), q05 = unname(stats::quantile(d, 0.05)), q95 = unname(stats::quantile(d, 0.95)), range_of_means = diff(range(x$summary$bias[rows])))
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()) |> purrr::list_rbind()
lines_runs <- observed_lines |>
  dplyr::left_join(simulated_lines, by = c("estimate", "method", "series", "n")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(series = dplyr::if_else(method %in% c("none", "canada"), "", series),
    order = match(paste(method, series), c("none ", "canada ", "threshold Fire emissions", "threshold Natural disturbance line", "threshold Burned area", "kyoto_line Natural disturbance line", "kyoto_area Burned area")))
lines_wide <- function(d) d |>
  dplyr::arrange(order, n) |>
  dplyr::transmute(estimate = factor(estimate, c("MODIS", "NBAC", "Canada")), Treatment = unname(treatment_names[method]), `Test series` = series,
    `Baseline (years)` = ifelse(method %in% c("none", "canada"), "", as.character(n)), order, n,
    positive = num(positive), mean = ifelse(is.na(bias), "", paste(num(bias), "±", num(sd))), half = ifelse(is.na(half_width), "", num(half_width, 0))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = estimate, values_from = c(positive, mean, half), values_fill = "", names_vary = "slowest", names_sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(order, n) |>
  dplyr::select(-order, -n)
lines_table <- lines_wide(dplyr::filter(lines_runs, n %in% c(13, 16, 27, 45) | method %in% c("none", "canada")))
names(lines_table) <- sub("^positive_(.*)$", "\\1, positive (Mt CO2e)", sub("^mean_(.*)$", "\\1, mean ± SD (Mt CO2e a year)", sub("^half_(.*)$", "\\1, 90% half width (Mt CO2e a year)", names(lines_table))))
lines_every <- lines_wide(lines_runs)
names(lines_every) <- names(lines_table)
readr::write_csv(lines_every, "03.outputs/TBL/or-baselines.csv")
area_baselines <- purrr::map(13:(2017 - min(series_of$NBAC$area$year)), function(n) {
  a <- series_of$NBAC$area
  base <- a$ha[in_window(a$year, n)]
  thr <- mean(base) + 2 * stats::sd(base)
  tibble::tibble(n, mean = mean(base), sd = stats::sd(base), threshold = thr, flagged = paste(a$year[a$year >= 2017 & a$ha > thr], collapse = ", "))
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()
ab <- \(n) dplyr::filter(area_baselines, n == !!n)
lr <- \(est, m, n, s = NULL) dplyr::filter(lines_runs, estimate == est, method == m, n == !!n, if (is.null(s)) TRUE else series == s)
lsim <- \(est, m, n) dplyr::filter(simulated_lines, estimate == est, method == m, n == !!n)
lsim_range <- \(est, m, col) range(dplyr::filter(simulated_lines, estimate == est, method == m)[[col]])
fmt_lt <- function(est, t) with(dplyr::filter(lines_tests, estimate == est, test == t),
  paste0("[F(", df1, ", ", df2, ") = ", formatC(F, format = "f", digits = 3, big.mark = ","), ", p ", fmt_p(p), "]"))
lsim_msd <- \(est, m, n) with(lsim(est, m, n), paste0(num(bias), " ± ", num(sd), " Mt CO~2~e a year (95 per cent confidence interval ", num(ci_low), " to ", num(ci_high), ")"))
lsens <- \(est, chk, ms) dplyr::filter(lines_sensitivity, estimate == est, check == chk, method %in% ms, n == 13)$bias
```

```{r}
#| label: accounts

trees_uncertainty <- function(ci_half_width) 0.524417 / 1.645006 * ci_half_width
buffer_table <- c(none = 0.25, `1` = 0.20, `2` = 0.15, `3` = 0.20, `1,2` = 0.10, `1,3` = 0.15, `2,3` = 0.10, `1,2,3` = 0.05)
trees_buffer <- function(mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) buffer_table[[mitigating]] + if (after_reversal) 0.05 else 0
kept <- function(ci_half_width, mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) 1 - trees_uncertainty(ci_half_width) - trees_buffer(mitigating, after_reversal)
break_even <- function(...) (1 - trees_buffer(...)) / (0.524417 / 1.645006)
years13 <- 2004:2016
base13 <- cbm$immediate[cbm$year %in% years13]
natural_years <- cbm$year[cbm$immediate > mean(base13) + 2 * stats::sd(base13)]
accounts <- national |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2012) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reference = year <= 2016, rule = dplyr::if_else(year %in% natural_years, human, net))
level_split <- sum(accounts$human[accounts$reference]) / 5
level_whole <- sum(accounts$net[accounts$reference]) / 5
level_rule <- sum(accounts$rule[accounts$reference]) / 5
credits <- accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(!reference) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year, `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = human, `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_split - human, 1),
    `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = net, `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_whole - net, 1),
    `Threshold rule emissions (Mt)` = rule, `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(level_rule - rule, 1))
split_pos <- credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
whole_pos <- credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
rule_pos <- credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
worst <- which.min(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])
bc_burned <- dplyr::filter(burned, province == "BC")
bc_base <- bc_burned$hectares[bc_burned$year %in% years13]
bc_threshold_ha <- mean(bc_base) + stats::sd(bc_base)
bc_ha <- \(y) bc_burned$hectares[bc_burned$year == y]
bc_natural_years <- intersect(natural_years, bc_burned$year[bc_burned$hectares > bc_threshold_ha])
bc_accounts <- province |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(bc_share, year, share), by = "year") |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2012) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reference = year <= 2016, rule = dplyr::if_else(year %in% bc_natural_years, human, net))
bc_level_split <- sum(bc_accounts$human[bc_accounts$reference]) / 5
bc_level_whole <- sum(bc_accounts$net[bc_accounts$reference]) / 5
bc_level_rule <- sum(bc_accounts$rule[bc_accounts$reference]) / 5
bc_credits <- bc_accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(!reference) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year, `Burned area share (%)` = round(100 * share, 1), `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = round(human, 1), `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_split - human, 1),
    `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = round(net, 1), `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_whole - net, 1),
    `Threshold rule emissions (Mt)` = round(rule, 1), `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(bc_level_rule - rule, 1))
bc_split_pos <- bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])
bc_rule_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Threshold rule reductions (Mt)"]])
account_levels <- c("Disaggregated", "Undisaggregated", "Threshold")
account_table <- function(d, levels) dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(Year = d$Year, Account = "Disaggregated", E = d[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]], CL = levels[1]),
  tibble::tibble(Year = d$Year, Account = "Undisaggregated", E = d[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]], CL = levels[2]),
  tibble::tibble(Year = d$Year, Account = "Threshold", E = d[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]], CL = levels[3])) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Year, factor(Account, account_levels))
credits_table <- account_table(credits, c(level_split, level_whole, level_rule)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(Year), Account, `Net emissions (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", E), `Five-year mean (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL), `Reduction (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL - E))
bc_table <- account_table(bc_credits, c(bc_level_split, bc_level_whole, bc_level_rule)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(bc_credits, Year, share = `Burned area share (%)`), by = "Year") |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(Year), Account, `Burned area share (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", share), `Net emissions (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", E),
    `Five-year mean (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL), `Reduction (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", CL - E))

set.seed(42)
sd_mt <- 16.6 * (44 / 12) / 1.96
simulate_reductions <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  level - (emissions + stats::rnorm(n, 0, sd_mt))
}
monte_carlo <- function(reference, series) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(series)), function(k) {
    draws <- simulate_reductions(reference, series$emissions[k])
    half <- (stats::quantile(draws, 0.95) - stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)) / 2
    data.frame(Year = series$year[k], mean = mean(draws), sd = stats::sd(draws), q05 = unname(stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)), q95 = unname(stats::quantile(draws, 0.95)), half = half, ci = half / abs(mean(draws)))
  }))
}
reference_split <- accounts$human[accounts$reference]
mc_split <- monte_carlo(reference_split, data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))
mc_whole <- monte_carlo(accounts$net[accounts$reference], data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))
mc_rule <- monte_carlo(accounts$rule[accounts$reference], data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]]))
blank_if_negative <- function(value, mean_reduction) ifelse(mean_reduction > 0, value, NA)
uncertainty <- data.frame(Year = mc_split$Year,
  `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_split$mean, 1), `Disaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_split$ci), mc_split$mean),
  `Disaggregated deduction (%)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * trees_uncertainty(mc_split$ci), 1), mc_split$mean),
  `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_whole$mean, 1), `Undisaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_whole$ci), mc_whole$mean),
  `Threshold rule reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_rule$mean, 1), `Threshold rule interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_rule$ci), mc_rule$mean),
  `Threshold rule deduction (%)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * trees_uncertainty(mc_rule$ci), 1), mc_rule$mean), check.names = FALSE)
over <- uncertainty[["Disaggregated deduction (%)"]] > 100
uncertainty_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::mutate(mc_split, Account = "Disaggregated"), dplyr::mutate(mc_whole, Account = "Undisaggregated"), dplyr::mutate(mc_rule, Account = "Threshold")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Year, factor(Account, account_levels)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(Year), Account, `Mean reduction (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", mean), `Standard deviation (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.1f", sd),
    `5th percentile (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.0f", q05), `95th percentile (Mt CO2e)` = sprintf("%.0f", q95), `Relative half width (%)` = ifelse(mean > 0, sprintf("%.0f", 100 * ci), ""),
    `Adjustment factor (%)` = ifelse(mean > 0, sprintf("%.1f", 100 * trees_uncertainty(ci)), ""))
after <- credits$Year > min(credits$Year[!split_pos])
shared <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99), function(rho) {
  ci <- mc_split$ci * sqrt(1 - rho)
  data.frame(`Shared share` = rho, `Interval, lowest (%)` = round(100 * min(ci[split_pos])), `Interval, highest (%)` = round(100 * max(ci[split_pos])),
    `Years keeping a credit` = sum(purrr::map2_dbl(ci, after, \(h, a) kept(h, after_reversal = a))[split_pos] > 0), check.names = FALSE)
}))
sh <- function(share, column) shared[[column]][shared[["Shared share"]] == share]
rho_needed <- max(1 - (purrr::map_dbl(after[split_pos], \(a) break_even(after_reversal = a)) / mc_split$ci[split_pos])^2)
simulate_period <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  total <- length(emissions) * level - rowSums(matrix(rep(emissions, each = n) + stats::rnorm(n * length(emissions), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  half <- unname((stats::quantile(total, 0.95) - stats::quantile(total, 0.05)) / 2)
  centre <- length(emissions) * mean(reference) - sum(emissions)
  c(total = centre, half = half, ci = half / abs(centre))
}
period_split <- simulate_period(reference_split, credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]])
period_rule <- simulate_period(accounts$rule[accounts$reference], credits[["Threshold rule emissions (Mt)"]])
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

From 2017 to 2024, Canada's reported net emissions and removals fell below their 2012 to 2016 mean in most years, but only with natural disturbances disaggregated. No study found had measured the disaggregation's effect on emission reductions, or the record length it needs. This study rebuilt Canada's natural disturbance emissions with the Tier 1 method of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change guidelines. Burned area came from Canada's National Burned Area Composite, 1972 to 2024, and a global satellite product, 2001 to 2024. Four treatments of natural disturbance were compared on the two rebuilt lines and Canada's own. The four were no disaggregation, Canada's current disaggregation method, and the threshold methods of Australia's inventory and the 2013 Kyoto Protocol Supplement. Both threshold methods excluded natural disturbance emissions in years over two standard deviations above the mean of a baseline of 13 to 45 years. The composite's line followed Canada's fire year emissions (Pearson correlation `r sprintf("%.3f", nbac_fire_r$estimate)`, p \< 0.001) but removed less after the fire. A longer baseline excluded no more fire years under Australia's method, because the early record held large fire years as well as quiet ones. In simulated fire histories under the Kyoto Protocol method, a baseline of 45 years instead of 13 halved the 90 per cent range of annual reductions. It fell from `r num(lsim("NBAC", "kyoto_area", 13)$half_width, 0)` to `r num(lsim("NBAC", "kyoto_area", 45)$half_width, 0)` million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent a year, with the expected reduction near zero. A longer burned area record therefore steadied the Kyoto Protocol method rather than excluding more wildfires.

# Introduction

The IPCC's 2006 Guidelines counted as anthropogenic all emissions and removals "occurring on 'managed land'", which the 2019 Refinement named the Managed Land Proxy [@ipcc2006guidelines, p. 1.5; @ogle2019generic, p. 2.67]. @kurz2018quantifying wrote that natural disturbances in Canada's managed forests "can result in large and highly variable emissions and subsequent removals that mask the impacts of management activities". In Europe, natural disturbance was lowering the forest sink [@ritter2025alarming; @linscheid2026forest]. Canada's 2026 inventory split its managed forest into two components that summed to the total, the "Total Anthropogenic Component; Reported" and the "Natural Disturbance Component; Tracked but Not Reported" [@eccc2026nir]. The United States also divided its forest carbon change among growth, land use change and natural disturbances such as fire [@woodall2015forest]. The 2019 Refinement offered every country the same voluntary division, and a 2024 IPCC expert meeting recorded that the total "must be reported" [@ogle2019generic, p. 2.68; @ipcc2024reconciling, p. 59].

Guidance from 2003 asked inventories to report every disturbance on managed land [@ipcc2003gpg, pp. 1.11, 3.27]. The 2013 Kyoto Protocol Supplement addressed natural disturbance because "The ‘signal’ of the impact of human activities ... may not be discernible against the ‘noise’ of large interannual variability" [@ipcc2014kp, p. 2.31]. The Supplement set natural disturbance emissions against a background level, for which countries were "encouraged to use the longest available time series" [@ipcc2014kp, p. 2.46]. Only the emissions above that level were excluded, and only in a year above it plus a margin of twice the standard deviation [@ipcc2014kp, pp. 2.49, 2.50]. The Supplement's first condition was that "There is no observed trend in natural disturbance emissions during the calibration period that is not considered in the background level estimation, or expected during the commitment period" [@ipcc2014kp, p. 2.50].

Before the 2019 Refinement, projections under future disturbance regimes showed that Canada's managed forest could be a net source [@kurz2008risk; @metsaranta2010implications]. Canada's inventory built its managed forest estimate with CBM-CFS3, the Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector [@kurz2009cbm; @stinson2011inventory]. Its 2017 edition first kept burned stands in a natural disturbance component, for a fixed 60 years [@eccc2017nir, p. 141; @kurz2018quantifying]. From the 2018 edition, the period was set by region, at 45 to 99 years and 76 on average [@eccc2018nir, p. 121; @eccc2026nir, p. 435]. The 2022 edition first took the National Burned Area Composite for every year from 1990 [@eccc2022nir, p. 152], after the composite was extended back to 1986 [@skakun2022extending]. The 2023 edition first delayed regrowth on part of each year's burned area, using "remote-sensing derived information" [@eccc2023nir, p. 156]. The 2024 edition first assigned the last stand-replacing disturbance before 1990 from provincial harvest records [@eccc2024nir, p. 165]. That revised harvest record cut the 1990 reported sink by 113 Mt CO~2~e, or 56 per cent [@kurz2024revised]. CBM-CFS3 still assumed "only high severity fires, despite evidence of widespread mixed-severity fires", and its regional emissions ran "typically 10 % to 25 % higher" than with severity from satellite maps [@thompson2026incorporating, p. 3617].

Where natural disturbances were disaggregated, records of different lengths set the threshold a fire year had to exceed. Australia's inventory classed a fire season as anomalous when national fire emissions exceeded the mean of a 2000 to 2012 baseline by two standard deviations [@bowman2023wildfire]. The European Union set its background level for 2021 to 2030 on the mean of 2001 to 2020, "excluding statistical outliers" [@eu2018regulation]. The European example in the 2019 Refinement, which "has not yet been implemented", started its series in 1971 and assumed recovery within 20 years [@ogle2019generic, pp. 2.76-2.77]. Its footnote noted that twice the standard deviation was "an approximation of Student’s t value for data series with number of data \>= 30" [@ogle2019generic, p. 2.77]. In 2023, Canada's fire season burned `r sprintf("%.1f", nbac_2023 / 1e6)` Mha on the National Burned Area Composite and emitted 647 Tg of carbon [@cfs2026nbac; @byrne2024carbon].

The 2019 uncertainty chapter advised caution "in cases where the point estimate is very small when compared with the size of the confidence interval" [@paciornik2019uncertainties, p. 3.19]. The CBM-CFS3 interval was 32.2 Tg C a year wide, which @metsaranta2017uncertainty stated "cannot be meaningfully expressed in percentage terms because its range of possible values contains zero". Regional carbon budgets for Australia, the Brazilian Amazon and California had the same difficulty [@haverd2013australian; @rosan2023contemporary; @divittorio2021quantifying]. ART TREES, the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard of the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions, credited national and subnational emission reductions against the mean emissions of five historical years [@art2026trees3, pp. 13, 33]. The standard stated that "Only anthropogenic emissions shall be considered", and its footnote based the exclusion of non-anthropogenic emissions on the 2019 Refinement's definition of natural disturbance [@art2026trees3, p. 43; @ogle2019generic, p. 2.69].

Fire emission estimates began from burned area, which sources mapped in different ways. The MCD64A1 product mapped burned area monthly from November 2000 at 500 m, using the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) on the Terra and Aqua satellites [@giglio2021mcd64a1]. The IPCC's 2013 Wetlands Supplement listed the MODIS burned area algorithm among satellite products that "have all enabled the derivation of burnt area data in near real-time" [@ipcc2014wetlands, p. 2.42]. Canada's National Burned Area Composite combined 30 m Landsat mapping and agency fire polygons, with coarser satellite data for fires neither mapped [@hall2020generating]. The composite was extended from 2004 back to 1986, with 81 per cent of the burned area from Landsat change detection [@skakun2022extending]. Landsat MSS mapping then extended it to 1972 [@skakun2024mapping; @cfs2026nbac]. In Siberia, four satellite burned area datasets differed up to fivefold, and official Russian data were typically under 10 per cent of the satellite estimates [@kukavskaya2013fire]. Global forest results from the IPCC Tier 1 defaults differed by about 40 per cent between the 2003 and 2006 guidance [@petrescu2012global]. The five southern European countries most affected by fire estimated burnt biomass by different methods, some of which could overstate or understate it [@chiriaco2013comparison]. In North America over 2010 to 2019, inventories, atmospheric inversions and process models disagreed on the net source, partly through what each counted as human [@poulter2026north]. This study compared its results with the estimates generated by the FAOSTAT algorithm [@fao2025fires].

A review of 426 articles on Canada's forest carbon found the inventory's treatment of natural disturbance central to that research [@smyth2024year]. The 2019 Refinement set no length for the record behind a natural disturbance test [@ogle2019generic]. Background papers to a 2009 IPCC expert meeting warned that short base periods "have the capacity to be unduly influenced by variability that diverges from trend" [@ipcc2010revisiting, p. 37]. They added that a longer accounting period "is by itself not sufficient to address temporal variability in natural disturbance regimes" [@ipcc2010revisiting, p. 43]. A review of forest accounting from Kyoto to Paris found factoring out natural effects "not sufficiently secured by currently discussed accounting rules" [@krug2018accounting]. No study found had compared disaggregation methods, or the record lengths behind them, on one national inventory. The nearest work compared Canada's reported series under different divisions of the managed forest [@kurz2024revised; @bysouth2024high], or applied the same model to European forests [@pilli2013application; @pilli2016modellingb]. Other work compared national inventories with independent estimates [@grassi2022carbon; @nyawira2024pantropical; @pilli2016modellinga], or mapped the risk of forest carbon loss without reference to an inventory [@wu2026global]. This study first applied the IPCC Tier 1 method to Canada's burned area by ecological zone and by stratum, and set its defaults beside higher tier national datasets. It then rebuilt the natural disturbance line at Tier 1 on two burned area records, the composite for 1972 to 2024 and MCD64A1 for 2001 to 2024. Four treatments of natural disturbance were compared on these two lines and on the line of Canada's 2026 national inventory. The four were no disaggregation, Canada's approach, the threshold rule of Australia's inventory and the background level method of the 2013 Kyoto Protocol Supplement. The threshold rule and background level ran on every baseline ending in 2016, from 13 years to the full length of each record. In fire histories simulated with management fixed, each treatment was judged by its expected net credits or debits and the 90 per cent range of its annual reductions [@ipcc2014kp, pp. 2.31, 2.50]. The ART TREES uncertainty deduction was applied only to show what a percentage interval did to a small reduction.

# Materials and Methods

## Fire emission estimates

Fire emissions at every tier followed Equation 2.27 of the 2006 Guidelines, and the tiers differed in their data [@ipcc2006guidelines, pp. 2.42-2.43]. The IPCC decision tree for fire led to Tier 3 where "detailed data on biomass burning" could be used in "advanced models or methods" [@ipcc2006guidelines, p. 2.44]. The tree led to Tier 2 where "country-specific activity data emission factors" existed, and otherwise to Tier 1 and "aggregate data and default emission factors". The estimates generated by the FAOSTAT algorithm covered forest, savanna and organic soil fires at Tier 1 [@fao2025fires]. The algorithm's note gave its burned area as the MCD64A1 pixels with uncertainty below 20 per cent, classed by the yearly MCD12Q1 land cover map [@fao2025fires; @giglio2021mcd64a1; @friedl2022mcd12q1]. The product's user guide defined that layer as the uncertainty in the day of burn, in days [@giglio2021userguide, p. 10]. Forest was classes 1 to 5 of the map's International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme legend and the savanna items classes 6 to 10. The method was rerun in Google Earth Engine for 2001 to 2024, within the note's 2015 Global Administrative Unit Layers boundary of Canada. As in the note, each forest pixel took its ecological zone's fuel from the IPCC biomass consumption table [@ipcc2006guidelines, pp. 2.45-2.46]. Each item's burned area, biomass and gases were compared with the estimates. The coefficients of the estimates, biomass burned over burned area and each gas over biomass burned, were recovered and compared with the IPCC biomass consumption and emission factor tables [@ipcc2006guidelines, pp. 2.45-2.47].

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 2.27** [Estimation of greenhouse gas emissions from fire]{.smallcaps}

$$L_{\text{fire}} = A \cdot M_{B} \cdot C_{f} \cdot G_{ef} \cdot 10^{-3}$$

Where\
$L_{\text{fire}}$ = amount of greenhouse gas emissions from fire, tonnes of each GHG e.g., CH~4~, N~2~O, etc.\
$A$ = area burnt, ha\
$M_{B}$ = mass of fuel available for combustion, tonnes ha^-1^\
$C_{f}$ = combustion factor, dimensionless\
$G_{ef}$ = emission factor, g kg^-1^ dry matter burnt

Reproduced from Chapter 2 of Volume 4 of the 2006 Guidelines, pages 2.42 to 2.43, with the notes under the terms omitted [@ipcc2006guidelines].
:::

Without data for M~B~ and C~f~, Tier 1 took a default for their product, biomass consumption [@ipcc2006guidelines, pp. 2.45-2.46]. The 2019 Refinement reissued the biomass consumption table with the same boreal and temperate rows [@ogle2019generic, pp. 2.52-2.53]. The Tier 1 uncertainty was propagated by Equations 3.1 and 3.2 of the uncertainty chapter [@paciornik2019uncertainties, pp. 3.18-3.19]. Each term's uncertainty was 1.96 times the printed standard error or standard deviation over its mean, and burned area was given none. The chapter called the propagation "reasonably accurate as long as the percentage uncertainty is less than approximately 30%" [@paciornik2019uncertainties, p. 3.18]. The fuel took the boreal and other temperate rows, and the emission factor the savanna and grassland row the algorithm's estimates used [@ipcc2006guidelines, pp. 2.45-2.47].

::: {custom-style="IPCC Equation"}
**EQUATION 3.1 (UPDATED)** [Combining uncertainties, Approach 1, multiplication]{.smallcaps}

$$U_{\text{total}} = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n} U_{i}^{2}}$$

**EQUATION 3.2 (UPDATED)** [Combining uncertainties, Approach 1, addition and subtraction]{.smallcaps}

$$U_{\text{total}} = \frac{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left(U_{i} \cdot x_{i}\right)^{2}}}{\left| \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_{i} \right|}$$

Where\
$U_{\text{total}}$ = the percentage uncertainty of the product or sum, half the 95 percent confidence interval over the total\
$U_{i}$ = the percentage uncertainty of each quantity\
$x_{i}$ = the quantities combined\
$n$ = the number of quantities combined

Adapted from Chapter 3 of Volume 1 of the 2019 Refinement, pages 3.18 to 3.19 [@paciornik2019uncertainties].
:::

The guidelines' default strata were the ecological zones of the Food and Agriculture Organization's 2010 map, listed in their forest land chapter [@ipcc2006guidelines; @fao2012gez]. Canada fell in `r xfun::numbers_to_words(nrow(gez))` ecological zones on land, `r sprintf("%.0f", sum(gez$mha[gez$gez_abbrev %in% c("Ba", "Bb", "BM")]))` Mha of them boreal (@fig-zones), and Online Resource 1 listed the Tier 1 defaults for each zone. Each zone took the rows of the IPCC biomass consumption, emission factor and combustion factor tables that its vegetation matched [@ipcc2006guidelines, pp. 2.45-2.49]. The 5 arc minute IPCC default soil raster gave eight classes, organic, sandy, wetland, volcanic, spodic, high activity clay, low activity clay and other [@batjes2010ipcc]. The MCD12Q1 map of 2023 kept its classes as the algorithm grouped them [@fao2025fires]. The Canadian National Fire Database gave each fire's cause, natural, human or unknown, its month and, where recorded, its type, crown, surface or ground [@cfs2026nfdb].
